title: General Bayesian Policy Learning
summary: This study proposes a General Bayes framework for policy learning. We consider decision problems in which a decision-maker chooses an action from a given set to maximize expected welfare. Typical examples include treatment choice and portfolio optimization. In such problems, the statistical target is a decision rule, and predicting each potential outcome is not necessarily of primary interest. We formulate this policy-learning problem through loss-based Bayesian updating. Our main technical device is a squared-loss surrogate for welfare maximization.
